title: Zanzibar Destination Wedding Plans That Begin With a Few Days in the Serengeti
meta_title: Zanzibar Destination Wedding Guide, Safari Included
meta_description: Plan a Zanzibar destination wedding with a safari: legal steps, best months, a 10-day route, group costs and logistics for your guests. Ask for a group quote.
excerpt: A Zanzibar destination wedding pairs a few days in the Serengeti and Ngorongoro with a beach ceremony. Here is how to plan the legal side, the route and the costs for your whole party.
content:
A Zanzibar destination wedding with a safari works best as a 9 to 11 day trip: three or four nights on Tanzania's northern circuit first, then a short flight to the island for the ceremony and a few slow beach days. Plan the legal side early, because official guidance asks for 21 days' notice of marriage.

The hard part is not the beach or the lions. It is moving 20 or 30 people of different ages, budgets and flight times through the parks and onto an island without anyone missing the big day. This guide covers the legal paperwork, the best months, a sample route, vehicles and rooming, rough costs and the small decisions that keep a wedding party happy. For trips built around a celebration, see our special occasion safaris for groups.

Quick Facts

  • Ideal length: 9 to 11 days: 3 or 4 safari nights, then 4 to 6 nights on Zanzibar
  • Best months: June to October and mid-December to February; avoid April and May
  • Group size: 12 to 40 guests is the usual range; six guests per safari vehicle
  • Legal notice: About 21 days before the ceremony, so many couples marry at home first
  • Getting there: Fly into Kilimanjaro, then about 1 to 1.5 hours from Arusha to Zanzibar
  • Insurance: Zanzibar inbound cover US$44 per adult (checked November 2026)

Why Pair a Zanzibar Destination Wedding With a Safari?

A safari gives a Zanzibar destination wedding something no beach resort can: a shared adventure in the days before the ceremony. Guests who barely know each other on arrival are swapping leopard photos by the rehearsal dinner, and the couple gets far more time with the people who flew halfway round the world for them.

It also makes the long journey worthwhile. Most guests will spend a full day travelling and may only visit East Africa once, so adding the Serengeti and the Ngorongoro Crater turns an expensive invitation into a trip of a lifetime.

There is a practical upside too. Northern Tanzania and Zanzibar sit in the same country, share one visa and are linked by daily scheduled flights, so a Zanzibar destination wedding with a safari needs no second border crossing.

Who usually comes on the safari part?

Not every guest joins the safari. A common pattern for a Zanzibar destination wedding is a core group of 10 to 20, often close family and the bridal party, who arrive early for the parks, while others fly straight to the island two or three days before the ceremony.

Can You Legally Marry in Zanzibar?

Yes, foreigners can legally marry in Zanzibar, but the paperwork takes time. You will need passports, birth certificates, a certificate of no impediment from home, proof that any earlier marriage has ended, two passport photos each and two witnesses, with English translations of anything in another language.

The US Embassy in Tanzania guidance on marriage says a notice must be posted about 21 days before a Zanzibar ceremony, and that documents should be notarised. A 2024 guide from a Zanzibar law firm describes a special licence for couples who cannot give that notice, so the rules are worth confirming directly with the registrar or through your resort before you set a date. Marriages are registered with the Zanzibar Civil Status Registration Agency.

Legal ceremony at home, celebration on the island

Because of the notice period and the document checks, many couples sign the legal papers at a registry office at home a week or two before travelling. The Zanzibar destination wedding then becomes a symbolic ceremony or blessing on the beach, led by a celebrant, with none of the stress of a missing stamp. Your guests will not notice the difference, and you avoid having your marriage certificate legalised for use back home.

If you want the legal ceremony itself to be part of your Zanzibar destination wedding, arrive a few days early, keep certified copies of every document, and ask your own embassy whether the Tanzanian certificate needs further attestation at home.

Visas and insurance for every guest

Every wedding guest needs a valid passport, in most cases a Tanzania visa, and the Zanzibar inbound travel insurance, which costs US$44 per adult and US$22 per child and must be bought online before arrival (checked November 2026). Our Tanzania visa guide explains the e-visa process step by step.

Zanzibar's policy is sold through the official Zanzibar inbound insurance portal. Mainland Tanzania added its own US$44 policy from 1 October 2026, and the mainland insurer says a policy bought at your first point of entry covers both, but confirm this for each guest's route before travel. Guests flying from Kenya or other countries where yellow fever is present may also be asked for a vaccination certificate.

Planning the Safari Leg for Your Wedding Guests

The safari leg of a Zanzibar destination wedding usually covers Tarangire, the Serengeti and the Ngorongoro Crater over three to five nights, starting in Arusha. That route keeps drives to a manageable length, shows guests the big cats, elephants and huge plains, and ends close to Arusha or a Serengeti airstrip for the flight to the coast.

Park fees are the fixed part of the budget. The Serengeti charges US$82 per adult per 24 hours including VAT, and taking a vehicle down into the Ngorongoro Crater adds a US$295 service fee per vehicle per descent (checked October 2026). Our guide to Tanzania park fees breaks down every northern park.

Sample 10-day Zanzibar destination wedding itinerary

This is a common shape for a Zanzibar destination wedding, with the ceremony on day 8 so guests can rest after the parks. Shorten the safari to three nights for guests with limited leave.

DayWhereWhat happens
1ArushaArrive at Kilimanjaro International Airport, transfer to a garden lodge, welcome drinks
2TarangireMorning drive to Tarangire for elephants and baobabs, sundowner at the lodge
3-4Central SerengetiFull days on the plains, optional sunrise balloon flight for the couple
5Ngorongoro CraterCrater floor game drive and picnic, night on the rim
6ZanzibarDrive to Arusha or fly from a Serengeti airstrip to Zanzibar, check in on the beach
7ZanzibarFree day, Stone Town walk or dhow cruise, rehearsal dinner
8ZanzibarWedding ceremony and reception
9-10ZanzibarRecovery breakfast, snorkelling, departures

When Is the Best Time for a Zanzibar Destination Wedding?

The best time for a Zanzibar destination wedding is June to October or mid-December to February. Both windows are mostly dry on the island and good for game viewing on the mainland. April and May are the long rains, when some beach resorts close, and November brings short, sharp showers.

MonthsZanzibarSafari leg
January-FebruaryHot and mostly dry, calm seasCalving season in the southern Serengeti
MarchHumid, rains startingGreen parks, fewer vehicles
April-MayLong rains, some resorts closeLowest prices, muddy roads; least suited to weddings
June-OctoberDry, breezy, cooler eveningsPeak game viewing; migration in the northern Serengeti from about July
NovemberShort rains, usually brief showersGood value, green landscapes
DecemberDrying out, busy over the holidaysHerds moving south; book early for Christmas dates

Two other calendars matter. Zanzibar is predominantly Muslim, and during Ramadan, expected to begin in early February in 2027, Stone Town is quieter and eating or drinking in public during daylight is frowned upon, although beach resorts keep running as normal. And peak weeks such as Christmas, New Year and August fill both safari lodges and resorts a year ahead. Our month-by-month guide to Tanzania has more detail on each park.

Vehicles, Rooming and Flights for a Wedding Party

A wedding party on safari is easiest to manage with six guests per Land Cruiser, so everyone has a window seat and a view through the pop-up roof. Twenty guests means four vehicles, each with its own guide, travelling as a loose convoy and meeting up at lunch stops and the lodge.

Rooming needs more thought than at a hotel. Safari lodges often have only 10 to 30 rooms, so a large Zanzibar destination wedding party may take a whole camp or split between two of the same standard. Ask early who needs a double, a twin or a single, as singles often carry a supplement.

Getting everyone from the bush to the beach

Scheduled light-aircraft flights link Arusha with Zanzibar in roughly one to one and a half hours, and flights from Serengeti airstrips take around two and a half to three and a half hours because they stop on the way (timetable checked November 2026). Flights usually leave late morning and land early afternoon. Luggage limits on these aircraft are tight, so wedding outfits are best carried in soft bags or sent ahead with the planner.

Guests who skip the safari can fly into Zanzibar directly, often through Dar es Salaam, Nairobi or a Gulf hub, and still arrive in good time for the Zanzibar destination wedding.

How Much Does a Zanzibar Destination Wedding With a Safari Cost?

A Zanzibar destination wedding with a four-night safari typically costs guests between about US$3,000 and US$8,000 per person excluding international flights, depending on lodge standard and season. These are rough estimates for planning; the wedding itself, from venue hire to flowers, is usually billed separately by the resort.

Budget tierSafari, 4 nights (estimate per person)Zanzibar, 4 nights (estimate per person)
Comfortable mid-rangeAbout US$1,800 to US$2,600About US$600 to US$1,200
UpmarketAbout US$2,800 to US$4,500About US$1,200 to US$2,500
LuxuryUS$5,000 and upUS$2,500 and up

These ranges include park fees, a private vehicle and guide, full-board safari lodges and a beach resort on half board. They exclude flights, visas, insurance, drinks, tips and the Zanzibar destination wedding package itself. Rates rise in July, August and over Christmas, and fall in March and November.

How group pricing helps the guest list

Groups often share costs well: four vehicles cost the same whether each carries five or six people, and the Ngorongoro crater fee is per vehicle, not per person. On our group trips, for every six paying travellers the seventh place is free, which many couples use for themselves or a parent. Guests can also pay their share separately, which saves the couple chasing money. Our page on how to organise a group safari explains deposits and payments.

Choosing a Venue and Planning the Island Days

Most Zanzibar destination wedding ceremonies take place at a beach resort. North and west-facing beaches catch the sunset, while the east coast faces the sunrise. Resorts handle the arch, seating, sound and catering, and many keep a list of local celebrants, florists and photographers.

Think about the tide. On the east coast the sea retreats a long way at low tide, which can leave a ceremony facing a wide flat instead of open water. The north coast around Nungwi and Kendwa is less affected, which is one reason it suits a sunset Zanzibar destination wedding.

Stone Town and the days around the wedding

Stone Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is a lovely half-day for guests: carved doors, spice markets and rooftop dinners. A walking tour the day before the wedding gives people something to do while the couple prepares. For more island ideas, read our guide to adding Zanzibar to a Tanzania safari.

Dress codes matter in town. Ask guests to cover shoulders and knees in Stone Town and villages; inside the resort, a Zanzibar destination wedding can look like a beach wedding anywhere, and alcohol is served as normal.

Insider Tips

  • Send a save-the-date early: Give guests 9 to 12 months, as peak-season lodges fill fast
  • Collect passport details once: One spreadsheet of names, dates of birth and flights saves days of emails
  • Book the couple a quiet night: Put the couple in a separate tent or suite the night before the ceremony
  • Plan a rest day: Leave at least one free day between the safari and the wedding
  • Pack outfits in hand luggage: Light aircraft limit bags, and a lost suit is hard to replace on the island
  • Check the tide table: Set the ceremony time around high tide on east coast beaches

Frequently Asked Questions

Can foreigners legally marry in Zanzibar?

Yes. Foreigners can legally marry in Zanzibar if they bring passports, birth certificates, a certificate of no impediment and proof that any earlier marriage has ended, with English translations where needed. Official guidance asks for notice about 21 days before the ceremony, so many couples marry at home first and hold a symbolic ceremony on the island instead.

How many guests suit a Zanzibar destination wedding with a safari?

Most Zanzibar destination wedding groups that add a safari number between 12 and 40 guests. Up to about 20 fits one or two lodges on the northern circuit with ease. Larger parties still work, but they usually split across two camps of the same standard or send some guests straight to the beach while a smaller group goes on safari.

Should the safari come before or after the wedding?

The safari usually comes first. Guests arrive at Kilimanjaro, spend three or four days in Tarangire, the Serengeti and the Ngorongoro Crater, then fly to Zanzibar for the wedding with a tan and stories to share. Ending on the beach also means nobody bounces along a dusty road the day after the celebration.

What is the best month for a Zanzibar destination wedding?

The best months for a Zanzibar destination wedding are June to October and mid-December to February, when the island is mostly dry and the northern parks are at their best for game viewing. April and May bring the long rains and some resorts close. Check Ramadan dates too, as Stone Town is much quieter then.

Do wedding guests need insurance and visas for Tanzania?

Yes. Most wedding guests need a Tanzania visa, and Zanzibar requires its own inbound travel insurance, at US$44 per adult (checked November 2026). Mainland Tanzania introduced a similar policy from 1 October 2026, and the insurer says one policy bought at your first point of entry covers both. Ask every guest to confirm the rules before booking.

Final Thoughts

A Zanzibar destination wedding with a safari asks more of the planning than a single resort, but your guests get game drives together and then a ceremony by the Indian Ocean. Sort the legal route first, pick a dry month and keep a rest day before the big day.
